translation_en: Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Abdullah ibn Yazid, the freedman of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Fatimah bint Qays, that Abu Amr ibn Hafs gave her an irrevocable divorce while he was away. His agent sent her some barley, which she disliked. He said, “By Allah, you are entitled to nothing from us.” She went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. He said, “You are not entitled to maintenance from him.” He told her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Sharik, then said, “That is a woman whom my companions visit often. Observe your waiting period at Ibn Umm Maktum’s, for he is blind and you may put aside your outer garments there. When your waiting period is over, inform me.” When it was over, she told him that Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to her. The Messenger of Allah said, “As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his stick down from his shoulder; as for Muawiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd.” I disliked that, but he said, “Marry Usamah.” I married him, and Allah placed good in him, and I was delighted with him.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz—Ibn Abi Hazim—narrated to us. Qutaybah also said: Ya‘qub—Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us. Both reported from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salamah, from Fatimah bint Qays, that her husband divorced her during the time of the Prophet and gave her inadequate maintenance. When she saw that, she said, “By Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah. If I am entitled to maintenance, I will take what is right for me; if I am not, I will take nothing from him.” She told the Messenger of Allah, and he said, “You are entitled neither to maintenance nor housing.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Abu Salamah, who said: I asked Fatimah bint Qays, and she told me that her Makhzumi husband divorced her and refused to maintain her. She went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. The Messenger of Allah said, “You are not entitled to maintenance. Move and go to Ibn Umm Maktum and stay with him, for he is blind and you may put aside your outer garments there.”

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya—Ibn Abi Kathir—who said: Abu Salamah informed me that Fatimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, informed him that Abu Hafs ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi divorced her three times, then went to Yemen. His family said, “You are not entitled to maintenance from us.” Khalid ibn al-Walid went with a group of men to the Messenger of Allah at Maymunah’s house. They said, “Abu Hafs divorced his wife three times; is she entitled to maintenance?” The Messenger of Allah said, “She is not entitled to maintenance, but she must observe the waiting period.” He sent her a message, “Do not get ahead of me with yourself.” He ordered her to move to Umm Sharik’s. Then he sent her another message: “The early Emigrants visit Umm Sharik, so go to the blind Ibn Umm Maktum, for when you put aside your head covering, he will not see you.” She went to him. When her waiting period ended, the Messenger of Allah married her to Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Harithah.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us: They said: Ismail—Ibn Ja‘far—narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Fatimah bint Qays. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: I wrote this directly from her dictation. She said: I was married to a man of Banu Makhzum, and he gave me an irrevocable divorce, so I sent to his family seeking maintenance. They related the story with the meaning of Yahya ibn Abi Kathir’s report from Abu Salamah, except that Muhammad ibn Amr’s report says, “Do not get ahead of us with yourself.”

Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both from Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d: My father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed him that Fatimah bint Qays informed him that she had been married to Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah. He gave her the final of three divorces. She said that she went to the Messenger of Allah seeking a ruling about leaving her house, and he ordered her to move to the blind Ibn Umm Maktum. Marwan refused to accept that a divorced woman could leave her house. Urwah said: Aishah objected to this report from Fatimah bint Qays.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated this to me: Hujayn narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, with the same chain and a similar report, including Urwah’s statement that Aishah objected to Fatimah’s report.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; these are Abd’s words. They said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Utbah, that Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah went with Ali ibn Abi Talib to Yemen. He sent his wife, Fatimah bint Qays, the remaining divorce from her divorces. He instructed al-Harith ibn Hisham and Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah to give her maintenance. They said to her, “By Allah, you are entitled to no maintenance unless you are pregnant.” She went to the Prophet and told him what they had said. He said, “You are not entitled to maintenance.” She asked his permission to move, and he permitted her. She said, “Where, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “To Ibn Umm Maktum.” He was blind, and she could put aside her clothes at his home without him seeing her. When her waiting period ended, the Prophet married her to Usamah ibn Zayd. Marwan sent Qabisah ibn Dhu’ayb to ask her about the hadith. She told him. Marwan said, “We have heard this hadith only from a woman. We will follow the established practice we found people upon.” When Fatimah heard what Marwan said, she replied, “The Quran is between me and you. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, ‘Do not turn them out of their houses…’” Quran 65:1. She said, “That applies to a woman whose husband may take her back. What applies after the third divorce? How can you say she has no maintenance if she is not pregnant? What, then, are you detaining her for?”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us: Sayyar, Husayn, Mughirah, Ash‘ath, Mujalid, Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, and Dawud informed us, all from al-Sha‘bi, who said: I entered upon Fatimah bint Qays and asked her about the Messenger of Allah’s ruling concerning her. She said, “My husband gave me an irrevocable divorce.” She said: I disputed with him before the Messenger of Allah about housing and maintenance. He did not grant me housing or maintenance and ordered me to observe my waiting period in Ibn Umm Maktum’s house.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, Dawud, Mughirah, Ismail, and Ash‘ath, from al-Sha‘bi, who said: I entered upon Fatimah bint Qays, with a report like Zuhayr’s from Hushaym.

Yahya ibn Habib narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us: Sayyar, Abu al-Hakam, narrated to us: al-Sha‘bi narrated to us: We entered upon Fatimah bint Qays. She treated us to fresh Ibn Tab dates and gave us a drink made from husked barley. I asked her, “Where does a woman divorced three times observe her waiting period?” She said, “My husband divorced me three times, and the Prophet gave me permission to observe my waiting period with my family.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Sha‘bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, from the Prophet, concerning a woman divorced three times: “She is entitled neither to housing nor maintenance.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated this to me: Yahya ibn Adam informed us: Ammar ibn Ruzayq narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha‘bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: My husband divorced me three times. I wanted to move, so I went to the Prophet, who said, “Move to the home of your cousin Amr ibn Umm Maktum and observe your waiting period there.”

Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jablah narrated this to us: Abu Ahmad narrated to us: Ammar ibn Ruzayq narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I was sitting with al-Aswad ibn Yazid in the central mosque, and al-Sha‘bi was with us. Al-Sha‘bi related the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, that the Messenger of Allah granted her neither housing nor maintenance. Al-Aswad took a handful of pebbles and threw them at him, saying, “Woe to you! You relate something like this?” He said, “Umar said: We will not abandon the Book of Allah and the practice of our Prophet for the statement of a woman, when we do not know whether she remembered or forgot. She is entitled to housing and maintenance. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, ‘Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a manifest indecency’” Quran 65:1.

Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Muadh narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, with this chain and a report like Abu Ahmad’s from Ammar ibn Ruzayq, including the story.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm ibn Sukhayr al-Adawi, who said: I heard Fatimah bint Qays say: My husband divorced me three times, and the Messenger of Allah granted me neither housing nor maintenance. The Messenger of Allah said to me, “When your waiting period is over, inform me.” I informed him, and Muawiyah, Abu Jahm, and Usamah ibn Zayd proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah said, “As for Muawiyah, he is poor and has no wealth. As for Abu Jahm, he strikes women often. Rather, marry Usamah ibn Zayd.” She gestured with her hand, saying, “Usamah? Usamah?” The Messenger of Allah said to her, “Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is better for you.” She said: I married him and was delighted.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm, who said: I heard Fatimah bint Qays say: My husband, Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah, sent Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah to deliver my divorce and sent with him five sa‘s of dates and five sa‘s of barley. I said, “Is this all the maintenance I have? And will I not observe my waiting period in your home?” He said, “No.” She said: I put on my clothes and went to the Messenger of Allah. He said, “How many times did he divorce you?” I said, “Three.” He said, “He has spoken truthfully; you are not entitled to maintenance. Observe your waiting period in the home of your cousin Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is blind and you may put aside your clothes there. When your waiting period ends, inform me.” She said: Several men proposed to me, including Muawiyah and Abu al-Jahm. The Prophet said, “Muawiyah is poor and in straitened circumstances; Abu al-Jahm is harsh with women”—or he said, “he strikes women,” or something similar—“but you should marry Usamah ibn Zayd.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abu Asim informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm narrated to me: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and I entered upon Fatimah bint Qays and asked her. She said: I was with Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah when he left for the expedition of Najran. He related a story like Ibn Mahdi’s report and added: She said, “I married him, and Allah honored me through Zayd’s son and ennobled me through Zayd’s son.”

Ubaydullah ibn Muadh al-Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Abu Bakr narrated to me: Abu Salamah and I entered upon Fatimah bint Qays during the time of Ibn al-Zubayr. She told us that her husband gave her an irrevocable divorce, with a report like Sufyan’s.

Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani narrated to me: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Hasan ibn Salih narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from al-Bahi, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: My husband divorced me three times, and the Messenger of Allah granted me neither housing nor maintenance.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham: My father said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id ibn al-As married the daughter of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam, then divorced her and made her leave his home. Urwah criticized them for that, but they said, “Fatimah left her home.” Urwah said: I went to Aishah and told her about it. She said, “There was no good for Fatimah bint Qays in mentioning this hadith.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Aishah, who said: “There was no good for Fatimah in mentioning this.” He said: She meant her statement, “There is neither housing nor maintenance.”

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said to Aishah, “Did you see so-and-so, daughter of al-Hakam? Her husband gave her an irrevocable divorce, and she left.” She said, “What a bad thing she did.” He said, “Did you not hear what Fatimah said?” She said, “There was no good for her in mentioning that.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: I said, “Messenger of Allah, my husband divorced me three times, and I fear that someone may break in upon me.” He ordered her to move.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj. Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us. Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me—these are his words—Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: My maternal aunt was divorced and wanted to harvest her date palms. A man rebuked her, telling her not to go out. She came to the Prophet, and he said, “Yes, harvest your date palms, for perhaps you may give charity or do some good.”

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me; their wording was close. Harmalah said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us. Abu al-Tahir said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas‘ud narrated to me that his father wrote to Umar ibn Abdullah ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhri, instructing him to visit Subay‘ah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah and ask her about her report and what the Messenger of Allah said when she sought a ruling. Umar ibn Abdullah wrote back to Abdullah ibn Utbah, informing him that Subay‘ah told him she had been married to Sa‘d ibn Khawlah, from Banu Amir ibn Lu’ayy and among those who had fought at Badr. He died during the Farewell Pilgrimage while she was pregnant. Soon after his death, she gave birth. When she had recovered from childbirth, she adorned herself for prospective suitors. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba‘kak, a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, entered upon her and said, “Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you hope to marry. By Allah, you cannot marry until four months and ten days have passed.” Subay‘ah said: When he told me this, I gathered my clothes together at evening and went to the Messenger of Allah to ask him about it. He ruled that I was free to marry as soon as I had given birth, and he told me that I could marry if I wished. Ibn Shihab said: I see no harm in her marrying as soon as she gives birth, even if she is still bleeding, provided her husband does not approach her until she becomes pure.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say: Sulayman ibn Yasar informed me that Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Abbas met at Abu Hurayrah’s and discussed a woman who gave birth a few nights after her husband died. Ibn Abbas said, “Her waiting period ends at the later of the two terms.” Abu Salamah said, “She is free to marry.” They disputed about it. Abu Hurayrah said, “I agree with my nephew”—meaning Abu Salamah. They sent Kurayb, Ibn Abbas’s freedman, to Umm Salamah to ask her about it. He returned and told them that Umm Salamah said: Subay‘ah al-Aslamiyyah gave birth a few nights after her husband died. She mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah, and he ordered her to marry.

Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated this to us: al-Layth informed us. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. Both reported from Yahya ibn Sa‘id with this chain, except that their report says, “They sent to Umm Salamah,” and does not name Kurayb.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Humayd ibn Nafi, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who informed him of these three hadiths. Zaynab said: I entered upon Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, when her father Abu Sufyan died. Umm Habibah called for perfume with yellow khaluq or something else, applied some to a servant girl, then rubbed it on her cheeks. She said, “By Allah, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah say from the pulpit, ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days.’” Zaynab said: I then entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh when her brother died. She called for perfume and applied some to herself, then said, “By Allah, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah say from the pulpit, ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days.’” Zaynab said: I heard my mother Umm Salamah say: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, my daughter’s husband has died, and her eye is sore. May we apply kohl to it?” The Messenger of Allah said, “No,” twice or three times, each time saying no. Then he said, “It is only four months and ten days. In pre-Islamic times, one of you would throw a piece of dung away at the end of a year.” Humayd said: I asked Zaynab, “What did she mean by throwing a piece of dung away at the end of a year?” Zaynab said: When a woman’s husband died, she would enter a small, shabby shelter, wear her worst clothes, and use no perfume or anything else until a year had passed. Then an animal—a donkey, sheep, or bird—would be brought to her, and she would rub herself against it. Rarely would she rub against anything without it dying. Then she would go out and be given a piece of dung, which she would throw away. After that she could use whatever perfume or other things she wished.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Nafi, who said: I heard Zaynab bint Umm Salamah say: A close relative of Umm Habibah died. She called for yellow perfume and rubbed it on her arms, saying, “I do this only because I heard the Messenger of Allah say, ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days, except for her husband: four months and ten days.’”
